q: The 'Human Development Index' for India in the 2021-22 Human Development Report was based on the data of the year:
explanation: The Human Development Report 2021-22, released in March 2022, used the 2019 data for the human development index because of the pandemic related data gaps.

q: The 'Global Hunger Index' 2022 placed India in the rank of:
explanation: In the Global Hunger Index 2022 India was ranked 131st out of the 136 countries covered, with a score of 16.8.

q: The 'Global Innovation Index' 2022 placed India in the rank of:
explanation: In the Global Innovation Index 2022 India was ranked 47th among 132 economies, in the 2023 index it improved to 43rd.

q: The 'World Air Quality Report' 2022 by IQAir placed India in the rank of:
explanation: In the 2022 World Air Quality Report, India was ranked between 101 and 150 among the countries with the cleanest air.

q: The 'World Happiness Report' 2022 was based on the survey data of the year:
explanation: The World Happiness Report 2022 used the Gallup World Poll data of 2021 and India was ranked at 140th.

q: The 'Ease of Doing Business' ranking of India before the World Bank discontinued the report in 2021 was:
explanation: In the Doing Business 2020 report India was ranked 63rd, and it was the first time it had entered the top 100, and the report was discontinued in 2021.

q: The 'Press Freedom Index' 2022 by Reporters Without Borders placed India in the rank of:
explanation: In the 2022 Press Freedom Index India was ranked 142nd, and in 2021 it was 142nd as well, with the report published on 3 May, the World Press Freedom Day.

q: The 'Global Gender Gap Report' 2022 of the World Economic Forum ranked India at:
explanation: In the Global Gender Gap Report 2022 India was ranked 129th, and it was the only country in the bottom 150 of the countries covered.

q: The 'Forest Survey of India' reported that as per the 2021 report, the forest and tree cover in India was about:
options: 25.17 per cent of the geographical area
18.33 per cent of the geographical area
29.48 per cent of the geographical area
21.76 per cent of the geographical area
explanation: The India State of Forest Report 2021 reported the forest and tree cover of 21.76 per cent of the geographical area, an increase of 1.89 percentage points over 2019.

q: The 'Multidimensional Poverty Index' 2022 of the UNDP and the OPHI was based on the survey of:
explanation: The Global MPI 2022 was based on the household surveys of 2019-20 conducted in India and it covered the deprivation in the health, the education and the living standards.

q: The 'SDG India Index' of the NITI Aayog for the year 2021-22 was based on the data of the year:
explanation: The SDG India Index 2021-22, prepared with the help of the Oxford Policy and Human Development Centre, used the district data of 2018-19.

q: The 'Environmental Performance Index' 2022 of Yale and Columbia placed India at the rank of:
explanation: In the Environmental Performance Index 2022 India was ranked 180th among 180 countries, and it was the second lowest in the air quality category.

q: The 'Global Peace Index' 2022 placed India in the rank of:
explanation: In the Global Peace Index 2022 India was ranked 135th, a drop from 126th in 2021, and in 2023 it was 134th.

q: The 'Democracy Index' of the Economist Intelligence Unit for 2021 placed India at:
explanation: In the Democracy Index 2021 India was ranked 48th with the score of 7.18, and India was classified as a 'flawed democracy'.

q: The 'World Competitiveness Ranking' of the World Economic Forum for 2021-22 placed India at:
explanation: In the World Competitiveness Ranking 2021-22 India was ranked 56th among 140 economies, and in 2022-23 it improved to 60th.

q: The 'World Energy Outlook' report of the IEA for 2021 focused on:
options: The energy sector and the net zero emissions pathway
explanation: The World Energy Outlook 2021 was the special report on the net zero emissions by 2050, and it was the first such report by the IEA.

q: The 'Economic Survey 2021-22' was titled:
explanation: The Economic Survey 2021-22 was titled 'Time to Move', and it was presented on 31 January 2022.

q: The 'Economic Survey 2020-21' was titled:
explanation: The Economic Survey 2020-21 was titled 'In the Union Budget 2021' and it was released on 29 January 2021.

q: The 'Economic Survey 2019-20' was titled:
explanation: The Economic Survey 2019-20 was titled 'India's Growth Roadmap' and it was presented on 14 January 2020.

q: The 'Padma Awards' are announced every year on:
explanation: The Padma Awards, the civilian awards of the Government of India, are announced on 26 January every year along with the Republic Day honours.

q: The 'Bharat Ratna' was first awarded in:
explanation: The Bharat Ratna, instituted in 1954, was first conferred on Dr. Radhakrishnan, Dr. C. Rajagopalachari and Dr. S. Radhakrishnan, and it was the 1954 award to the philosopher Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan and C. Rajagopalachari.

q: The Nobel Prize in Literature for 2022 was awarded to:
explanation: The Nobel Prize in Literature for 2022 was awarded to the Norwegian playwright Jon Fosse, and the 2021 prize went to Abdulrazak Gurnah.

q: The Nobel Peace Prize for 2022 was awarded to:
options: Ales Bialiatski and the Memorial and the Centre for Civil Liberties
Abiy Ahmed and the Ethiopian Peace
explanation: The Nobel Peace Prize for 2022 was shared by Ales Bialiatski of Belarus and the Russian Human Rights Foundation, the Memorial and the Centre for Civil Liberties, while the 2021 prize went to Maria Ressa and Dmitry Muratov.

q: The Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences for 2022 was awarded to:
options: Ben Bernanke, Douglas Diamond and Philip Dybvig
Claudia Goldin and James Heckman and Michael Katz
Esther Duflo and Abhijit Banerjee and Michael Kremer
explanation: The 2022 prize in Economic Sciences was awarded to Ben Bernanke, Douglas Diamond and Philip Dybvig for their work on the banks and the financial crises, while the 2023 prize went to Claudia Goldin, James Heckman and Michael Katz.

q: The Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences for 2023 was awarded to:
options: Esther Duflo, Abhijit Banerjee and Michael Kremer
Ben Bernanke and Douglas Diamond and Philip Dybvig
Claudia Goldin, James Heckman and Michael Katz
explanation: Claudia Goldin, James Heckman and Michael Katz shared the 2023 prize for their empirical work on the inequality and the institutions.

q: The Nobel Prize in Physics for 2022 was awarded to:
options: Alain Aspect, John Clauser and Anton Zeilinger
Klaus Hasselmann and Syukuro Manabe and Giorgio Parisi
Didier Queloz and Michel Mayor and David Wineland
Ashvin A. Parmar and K. Barry Sharpless and Richard F. Schrock
explanation: The 2022 Physics prize went to Alain Aspect, John Clauser and Anton Zeilinger for the experiments with the entangled photons and the establishment of the violation of the Bell inequalities.

q: The Nobel Prize in Chemistry for 2022 was awarded to:
options: Carolyn Bertozzi, Morten Meldal and Barry Sharpless for the click chemistry and the bioorthogonal chemistry
explanation: The 2022 Chemistry prize was awarded to Carolyn Bertozzi, Morten Meldal and Barry Sharpless for the development of the click chemistry and the bioorthogonal reactions, while the 2023 prize went to the discovery of the quantum dots and the synthesis of the quantum dots.

q: The Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for 2022 was awarded to:
options: Katalin Karikó and Drew Weissman for the nucleoside base modifications
Harvey Alter and Michael Houghton and Charles Rice
explanation: The 2022 Medicine prize was awarded to Katalin Karikó and Drew Weissman for their discoveries concerning the nucleoside base modifications that enabled the effective mRNA vaccines.

q: The World Food Prize for 2022 was awarded to:
options: Bono and The Beast of the Brothers
Ramesh Rajasingham and the Green Transformation Foundation
explanation: The World Food Prize for 2022 was awarded to Modadugu Gupta of India and the CIMMYT for their work in the development of the quality seeds of the wheat, and the 2023 prize went to Ramesh Rajasingham and the Green Transformation Foundation of the United States.

q: The 'Right Livelihood Award' for 2022 was given to:
options: Clymrar and the Accept Education group
explanation: The Right Livelihood Award for 2022 was given to the Accept Education group of Myanmar, and the 2023 award went to the Campaign for Nuclear Disarmament, the Centre for Health and the Environment and the Brazilian movement for the rights of the people of the Amazon.

q: The 'Ramon Magsaysay Award' for 2022 was given to:
options: Sandeep Pandey and the Climate of Change Trust
Sandeep Pandey and the Asianet and the MTF
explanation: The Ramon Magsaysay Award for 2022 was given to Sandeep Pandey of the Climate of Change Trust, and the 2023 award went to the Seruan-Dek Project and the Ahilan Trust.

q: The 'Sahitya Akademi Award' for 2022 in the English language was given to:
explanation: Girish Karnad received the Sahitya Akademi Award for the English for his novel Yakshagana in 2022, and the 2021 award went to Manilal H. Patel for Audition.

q: The 'Jnanpith Award' for 2022 was given to:
explanation: The Jnanpith Award for 2022 was given to the Malayalam writer D. Murali and the Sanskrit scholar Jagadguru Rambhadracharya, and the 2021 award went to Nilamani Phookan for his poetry.

q: The 'Dadasaheb Phalke Award' for 2022 was given to:
options: Waheeda Rehman for the contribution to Indian cinema
explanation: The Dadasaheb Phalke Award for 2022 was given to Waheeda Rehman for her contribution to Indian cinema, and the 2021 award went to Rajkummar Rao.

q: The 'National Film Award for the Best Feature Film' of 2021 was given to:
explanation: The National Film Award for the Best Feature Film at the 69th ceremony went to The Rocket, a Malayalam film, and the 70th awards in 2022 went to Rocketry and Sita Ramam.

q: The 'Arjuna Award' in the major disciplines of the Games for 2022 was given to:
options: Neeraj Chopra, Ravindra Jadeja, Pramod Bhagat and the others
explanation: At the 2022 Asian Games, Neeraj Chopra won the javelin gold, and the Indian team won the men's cricket gold with the Arjuna Awards going to the members of the squad.

q: India's medals at the Tokyo 2020 Olympic Games:
options: One gold, one silver and two bronze
explanation: At the Tokyo 2020 Olympics, held in 2021, India won one gold (Sushil Kumar), one silver (Ravi Kumar Dahiya) and two bronze (Paddlers), for a total of four medals.

q: The Indian medals at the Paris 2024 Olympic Games:
explanation: At the Paris 2024 Games India won one silver, in the men's archery individual compound, by the archer Dharashree Verma, and five bronze medals for a total of six.

q: The 'Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award' for 2022 was conferred on:
options: Neeraj Chopra, Pramod Bhagat, Deepika Kumari, Ravi Kumar Dahiya, Sunil Chhetri and others
Pramod Bhagat and the badminton players only
explanation: The Khel Ratna Award for 2022 was conferred on Neeraj Chopra, Pramod Bhagat, Deepika Kumari, Ravi Kumar Dahiya, Sunil Chhetri, Harmanpreet Singh and Lovlina Borgohain.

q: The Khel Ratna Award was renamed the:
options: Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award from the beginning
explanation: The Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna Award, the highest sporting honour in India, was renamed the Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award in 2021.

q: The 'ICC Men's Cricket World Cup 2023' was won by:
explanation: Australia won the 2023 ICC Men's Cricket World Cup, defeating India in the final at the Ahmedabad on 19 November 2023.

q: The 'ICC T20 World Cup 2024' was won by:
explanation: South Africa won the ICC T20 World Cup 2024, which was the first men's T20 World Cup title for the Proteas, and the tournament was held in the West Indies and the USA.

q: The 'Commonwealth Games 2022' were held in:
explanation: The 2022 Commonwealth Games were held in Birmingham in England, with India winning the medal table with 19 gold medals and 57 medals in all.

q: The 'Asian Games 2022' were held in:
explanation: The 19th Asian Games were held in Hangzhou in China in October 2023, and India won 19 gold medals and 38 medals in all.

q: The 'Formula 1' Indian Grand Prix returned to India in 2022 after:
explanation: The Indian Grand Prix returned to the Buddh International Circuit in 2022 after a gap of six years, having been held in 2011 and 2014 as well.

q: The 'Vijay Amritraj' won the ATP Challenger title and the 'Bharat Ratna' in sports?
options: Vijay Amritraj was the first Indian Grand Prix winner
Vijay Amritraj won the Davis Cup for India
Vijay Amritraj was the first Indian to be ranked in the top ten of the ATP
explanation: Vijay Amritraj was the first Indian to be ranked among the top ten of the ATP singles and he won the Davis Cup for India in 1982 and in 1989.

q: The 'Dronacharya Award' is given for:
explanation: The Dronacharya Award is the national honour for the coaches in the sports and it was instituted in 1985.

q: The 'Arjuna Award' is given for:
options: The lifetime contribution to the sports
The outstanding performance in the sports over four years
explanation: The Arjuna Award, instituted in 1985, is given for the outstanding performance in the sports over the four years preceding the award.

q: The 'Sachar Committee' report and the 'hockey' and the 'Sher-e-Punjab':
options: The Sher-e-Punjab was the Indian team of the 1948 Olympics
The Sher-e-Punjab was the Indian hockey team of 1928
The Sher-e-Punjab was the India team of the 1932 Olympic hockey gold
The Sher-e-Punjab was the football team of 1936
explanation: The Indian hockey team of the 1932 Los Angeles Olympics, the first to win an Olympic gold for India, was known as the Sher-e-Punjab, and the Sachar Committee of 1935 recommended the measures for the reform of the game.

q: The 'Davis Cup' in 2021 was won by:
explanation: Russia won the Davis Cup in 2021 and 2020, and Croatia won it in 2018 and in 2019, while the United States holds the record with 32 titles.

q: The 'Indian Premier League' was founded in:
explanation: The Indian Premier League was founded in 2008 and the first season was won by the Rajasthan Royals, and it is the most valuable cricket league in the world.

q: The 'Pragati Maidan' and the 'Siri Fort' and the 'Kartavya Path':
options: The Kartavya Path corridor of the government buildings in Delhi
explanation: The Kartavya Path is the renovated central vista of the government offices in Delhi between the Rashtrapati Bhavan and the India Gate, and it was inaugurated in September 2022.

q: The 'Jal Jeevan Mission' aims to provide:
options: A functional household tap connection to every rural home
explanation: The Jal Jeevan Mission, launched in 2019, aims to provide a functional household tap water connection to every rural household, and the aim is the 55 litres per person per day of the prescribed quality.

q: The 'PM-KISAN' provides:
options: An income support of Rs. 6,000 per year to the landholding farmer families
A loan of Rs. 6,000 to the farmers
A subsidy of Rs. 6,000 on the seeds
explanation: The PM-KISAN scheme, launched in 2019, provides an income support of Rs. 6,000 per year in three equal instalments to the landholding farmer families.

q: The 'PM Fasal Bima Yojana' was launched in:
explanation: The Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana was launched in 2016 and it provides the crop insurance cover to the farmers with the premium paid by the government.

q: The 'Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana' provides:
options: The LPG connection to the women from the below poverty line households
explanation: PMUY, launched in 2016, provides the deposit-free LPG connection with a subsidised first refill and the support of the targeted subsidies to the women from the below poverty line and the SC/ST households.

q: The 'Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana' (Gramin) was launched in:
explanation: The PMAY-G was launched in 2015-16 with the aim of a pucca house to every rural household that does not have one, and the urban component was launched in 2015-16 as well.

q: The 'Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY' was launched in:
explanation: The Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY, the world's largest health assurance scheme, was launched on 23 September 2018 and it covers 5 crore families.

q: The 'PM Vishwakarma' scheme was launched in:
explanation: The PM Vishwakarma scheme was launched in November 2023 for the support of the 18 traditional craft trades with the credit, the training and the toolkit.

q: The 'PM SVANidhi' scheme was launched in:
explanation: The PM SVANidhi, the street vendors' livelihood support scheme, was launched in June 2020 during the pandemic with the collateral-free working capital loans.

q: The 'PM Gati Shakti' National Master Plan was approved in:
explanation: The PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan, with a ₹10 lakh crore outlay, was approved in October 2021 to develop the logistics and the infrastructure corridors.

q: The 'PM Kisan Maandhan Yojana' provides:
options: A pension of Rs. 3,000 per month to the small and marginal farmers
explanation: The PM KMY, launched in 2019, provides a monthly pension of Rs. 3,000 to the small and the marginal farmers on contribution and with a matching government contribution.

q: The 'Sukanya Samriddhi' scheme is for:
options: The girl child below the age of 10
explanation: The Sukanya Samriddhi account is a small savings scheme for the girl child below the age of ten and it offers one of the highest interest rates of the small savings schemes.

q: The 'Beti Bachao Beti Padhao' was launched in:
explanation: The Beti Bachao Beti Padhao campaign was launched on 5 May 2015 to address the sex-selective abortion and to promote the survival, the protection and the education of the girl child.

q: The 'Sampoorna Suraksha' and the 'POSHAN 2' were:
options: The Poshan 2 Abhiyaan and the universal immunisation programme
explanation: The POSHAN 2 Abhiyaan, the revised POSHAN or the Mid-Day Meal scheme, was launched in 2018-19 and the Sampoorna Suraksha, the universal immunisation programme, was launched in 2018.

q: The 'Namami Gange' programme was launched in:
explanation: The Namami Gange programme was launched in June 2009 as the National Ganga River Basin Authority programme to clean the Ganga and the tributaries.

q: The 'Swachh Bharat Mission' (rural) was launched in:
explanation: The Swachh Bharat Mission was launched on 2 October 2014 with the objective of the elimination of the open defecation and the construction of the toilets.

q: The 'One Stop Centre' for the women and the 'Sakhi' and the 'Samarthya':
options: The Samarthya is the skill development scheme
The Samarthya is the health insurance
The Samarthya is the food security scheme
The Samarthya programme is the One Stop Centre for the women, the children and the adolescents
explanation: The Samarthya, the One Stop Centre scheme of the Ministry of Women and Child Development, provides the integrated support to the women, the children and the adolescents in the districts.

q: The 'Ujjwala 2.0' and the 'LPG connection' in the scheme:
options: The PMUY 2.0 is only for the urban areas
The PMUY 2.0 is a loan scheme
The PMUY 2.0 was approved in 2021 and extended the benefits to the additional beneficiaries
explanation: The PMUY 2.0 was approved in 2021 and it extended the coverage with an additional deposit-free LPG connection, the first refill and the support of the targeted subsidies to the additional beneficiaries.

q: The 'Mission LiFE' was launched at:
explanation: The Mission LiFE was formally launched by the Prime Minister at the COP26 in Glasgow in November 2021 with the theme of 'LiFE' for the Lifestyle for Environment.

q: The '500 GW' non-fossil energy capacity target of India is to be achieved by:
explanation: India has committed to the 500 GW of installed non-fossil fuel based energy capacity by 2030 and to the net zero by 2070 at the COP26.

q: The 'LiFE' and the 'mission' of the '3 Ts':
options: The Mindful Consumption, the Value of the Time and the Value of the Money
The Transport, the Trade and the Tourism
The Technology, the Trade and the the Taxes
The Trees, the Temperature and the Territory
explanation: The Mission LiFE is built on the three core elements of the mindful consumption, the value of the time and the value of the money, centred on the demand-side approaches.

q: The 'PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana' was launched in:
explanation: The PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana, with a budget outlay of Rs. 75,021 crore, was launched in February 2024 to provide the rooftop solar to one crore households.

q: The 'National Green Hydrogen Mission' was approved with an outlay of:
explanation: The National Green Hydrogen Mission, approved in January 2023, has an outlay of Rs. 19,744 crore with a target of a minimum of 5 million tonnes of the annual green hydrogen production by 2030.

q: The 'COP27' of 2022 was held in:
options: Sharm el-Sheikh in Egypt and the Loss and Damage Fund was agreed
explanation: The COP27 at Sharm el-Sheikh in November 2022 agreed the Loss and Damage Fund and the commitment to phase down the coal power, and the 2023 COP28 at Dubai launched the Global Stocktake.

q: The 'COP28' at Dubai in 2023:
options: Agreed the Loss and Damage Fund
Was the first COP in Africa
Launched the first Global Stocktake and the transition away from the fossil fuels
explanation: The COP28 at Dubai in December 2023 completed the first Global Stocktake and called for the transition away from the fossil fuels in the energy systems.

q: The 'COP29' of 2024 was held in:
explanation: The COP29 was held in Baku in November 2024, and the new collective quantified goal on the climate finance of at least $300 billion a year by 2035 was agreed.

q: The 'COP30' of 2025 is scheduled to be held in:
explanation: The COP30 is scheduled to be held in Belem in Brazil in November 2025, in the Amazon region.

q: The 'India' and the 'Ramsar sites' in 2022 included:
options: The Deepor Beel and the Sultanpur
The Bhitarkanika Mangroves and the Vembanad
explanation: Among the Ramsar sites designated in 2022 were the Bhitarkanika Mangroves of Odisha, the Vembanad of Kerala, the Nang Chappa in Manipur and the Anamudi in Kerala.

q: The 'IUCN Red List' of 2022 and the 'Great Indian Bustard':
options: The Great Indian Bustard was listed as Endangered
The Great Indian Bustard was listed as Vulnerable
The Great Indian Bustard was removed from the list
The Great Indian Bustard was listed as Critically Endangered
explanation: The Great Indian Bustard was moved to the Endangered category in the IUCN Red List in 2022, and the 2020 assessment had also put it in the Endangered category.

q: The 'Chandrayaan-3' landing on 23 August 2023 was at:
options: The far side of the Moon
The south polar region of the Moon
The equatorial region of the Moon
The north polar region of the Moon
explanation: The Chandrayaan-3's Vikram lander touched down at around 69 degrees south latitude, near the lunar south pole, on 23 August 2023.

q: The 'Aditya-L1' was launched on:
explanation: The Aditya-L1 was launched on 1 July 2023 on a PSLV-C44 from Sriharikota and it was inserted into the halo orbit around the Lagrange point L1.

q: The 'Chandrayaan-2' was launched on:
explanation: The Chandrayaan-2 was launched on 22 July 2019 on a GSLV Mk III and the Vikram lander failed on 6 September 2019.

q: The 'Mangalyaan' reached the Mars orbit on:
explanation: The Mangalyaan entered the Mars orbit on 24 September 2014, and India became the first country to reach Mars on the first attempt.

q: The 'INS Vikrant' was commissioned in:
explanation: The INS Vikrant, the first indigenous aircraft carrier, was commissioned on 2 September 2022 by the President Droupadi Murmu.

q: The 'Astra Missile' was successfully test fired in 2021-2022 by:
explanation: The DRDO successfully test fired the Astra missile, the first made in India for the air-to-air combat, in November 2021 and again in July 2022.

q: The 'Indigenous' and the 'BrahMos' and the 'Akash' and the 'Mission Shakti' of 2019:
options: The Mission Shakti was the ASAT test that destroyed a satellite in the orbit
The Mission Shakti was the manned mission
The Mission Shakti was the nuclear test
The Mission Shakti was the mission to Venus
explanation: The Mission Shakti of March 2019 was the anti-satellite test in which the DRDO destroyed a satellite in the low earth orbit with the Microsat-R and the ASAT missile.

q: The 'Covaxin' was developed by:
explanation: Covaxin, the inactivated whole virion vaccine against COVID-19, was developed by the Bharat Biotech in Hyderabad, while Covishield was by the Serum Institute of India.

q: The 'covaccine' drive of India began on:
explanation: The nationwide CoWIN led vaccination drive began on 1 May 2021 with the vaccination of the frontline workers, and the 18 years and above were covered from 1 May.

q: The 'National Genome Sequencing Project' of India:
options: Was launched in 2005 for the rice genome
Was the Human Genome Project of 2003
Was launched in 2021 to map the SARS-CoV-2 variants
explanation: The National Genome Sequencing Project was launched in December 2021 to sequence the SARS-CoV-2 genomes and to track the variants circulating in India.

q: The 'BRICS' summit of 2023 was held in:
explanation: The 15th BRICS summit was held in Johannesburg in November 2023, and the 2024 summit was at Kazan in Russia, and India hosted the 2021 summit at Goa.

q: India hosted the BRICS summit in 2021 at:
explanation: India hosted the 14th BRICS summit at Goa in September 2021, the first in person after the pandemic, and the theme was 'Building on the BRICS spirit of the planet, peace, friendship and cooperation'.

q: The 'G20 Summit' of 2023 was held in:
explanation: The G20 summit of 2023 was held in New Delhi on 9 and 10 September with the theme of 'One Earth, One Family, One Future' and the Delhi Declaration was adopted.

q: The 'United Nations' and the 'General Assembly' and the '2022' session:
options: The 77th General Assembly was held in New York in September 2022
The 77th General Assembly was held in Buenos Aires
The General Assembly was held in Mumbai
The General Assembly was cancelled in 2022
explanation: The 77th General Assembly of the UN opened on 13 September 2022 in New York, and the UNGA was held in the person for the first time since 2019.

q: The 'UNSC Resolution 2728' of 2023:
options: Authorised the use of force in the Syria
Demanded the ceasefire in the Gaza and the humanitarian assistance
Established the peacekeepers in the Haiti
explanation: The UN Security Council Resolution 2728 of 15 November 2023 demanded the ceasefire in the Gaza and the protection of the humanitarian assistance, with the abstention of the United States.

q: The 'India' and the 'International Solar Alliance' was launched in:
explanation: The International Solar Alliance was launched on 30 November 2015 at the COP21 in Paris by the Prime Minister of India and the President of France.

q: The 'India' and the 'Global Alliance for Food Security' was launched in:
explanation: The Global Alliance for Food Security, with the G20 as the initiator, was launched in 2021 and the United States assumed the coordination of the Alliance.

q: The 'India' and the '2+2 dialogue' and the 'Quad' in 2022:
options: The Quad summit was in Tokyo in 2022
The Quad met in Paris in 2022
The Quad Leaders Summit was held in Bali in November 2022
The Quad summit was in Washington in 2022
explanation: The Quad Leaders' Summit was held in Bali in November 2022, and the first in person Quad summit was in Washington in September 2021.

q: The 'India' and the 'Voice of Global South Summit' was held in:
explanation: The first Voice of Global South Summit, with the theme of 'Partnership for a Debt-free and Sustainable Future', was held in New Delhi in January 2023.

q: The 'India' and the 'UAE' and the 'CEPA' of 2022:
options: The CEPA was with the UAE in 2005
The India-UAE CEPA was signed on 3 February 2022
explanation: The India-UAE Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement was signed on 3 February 2022, and it was the first CEPA that India signed with a partner country in two decades.

q: The 'India' and the 'Australia' and the 'ECPA' of 2020:
options: The India-Australia Economic Cooperation and Trade Agreement was signed on 2 October 2020
explanation: The India-Australia ECTA was signed on 2 October 2020, and it was the first trade agreement that India signed with a developed country in more than a decade.

q: The 'International Solar Alliance' and the 'Africa' and the 'Global South':
options: The ISA and the Global South are the institutional outcomes of the Indian diplomacy
The ISA is a NATO body
The Global South is a trade bloc
The ISA was founded by the United States
explanation: The International Solar Alliance and the Voice of Global South are the prominent institutional outcomes of the Indian diplomacy of the 2010s.

q: The 'India' and the 'UN' and the 'Security Council' reforms:
options: India is a member of the P5
India is a member of the G4 and the IBSA groups that campaign for the reform of the UNSC
India is a permanent member of the UNSC
explanation: India is a member of the G4, the Uniting for Consensus, the L69 and the IBSA, all of which campaign for the reform of the Security Council, and India has been a non-permanent member since 1950.

q: The 'India' and the 'World Bank' and the 'rise' of the 'South Asia':
options: The World Bank's South Asia and the regional development
The World Bank's loan for the dams
explanation: The World Bank's South Asia and the regional integration of the economies of South Asia is one of the areas of the cooperation with the rising economies.

q: The 'CAG' and the 'Copenhagen' and the 'Green Hydrogen':
options: It was launched at the COP27
It was launched in Delhi in 2021
It was launched in Paris in 2015
The Green Hydrogen Alliance was launched at the COP26 in Glasgow
explanation: The Green Hydrogen Alliance was launched by India, Denmark, Norway, the European Union and the European Investment Bank at the COP26 in Glasgow in 2021.

q: The 'United States' and the 'Inflation Reduction Act' of 2022:
options: It is the largest climate and the clean energy legislation in the history of the United States
explanation: The Inflation Reduction Act of August 2022, with about $369 billion for the climate and the clean energy, is the largest such legislation in the history of the United States.

q: The 'Energy Transition Index' of the World Economic Forum for 2022:
options: Was published for the first time in 2022 with India at the 132nd place
Was a report of the IEA on the coal
explanation: The World Energy Transition Index was published for the first time in 2022, and India was ranked 132nd in it.

q: The 'Stook' and the 'Climate Bonds' and the 'green bonds':
options: The green bonds are the loans to the farmers
The green bonds are the sanctions
The green bonds are the coal royalties
The green bonds are the debt instruments for the climate projects
explanation: The Climate Bonds Initiative classifies the green bonds as the fixed income instruments used to raise the money for the climate related projects.

q: The 'Biodiversity' and the 'Kunming-Montreal' agreement of 2022:
options: Was the CBD COP15 agreement on the targets for 2030
explanation: The Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework was adopted at the COP15 of the CBD at Kunming in December 2022, with the targets of protecting 30 per cent of the land and the sea by 2030.

q: The 'India' and the 'BBNJ' agreement:
options: The Agreement on the Marine Biodiversity of the Areas Beyond National Jurisdiction was adopted in 2023
explanation: The BBNJ agreement, the high seas treaty, was adopted in June 2023 to establish the marine protected areas in the areas beyond the national jurisdiction.

q: The 'India' and the 'Plastic' and the 'Single-use plastic' ban:
options: The ban came into effect in 2019
The ban on the identified single-use plastic items came into effect on 1 July 2022
explanation: The ban on the identified single-use plastic items came into effect on 1 July 2022, and the plastic waste management rules of 2016 had banned the identified items earlier.

q: The 'Extended Producer Responsibility' for the plastic packaging:
options: Was notified in 2022 with the targets for the recycling and the EPR
explanation: The EPR Guidelines for the plastic packaging were notified in March 2022 with the targets for the recycled content and the plastic waste management.

q: The 'Biodegradable' and the 'compostable' packaging:
options: The Government notified the quality standards for the biodegradable and the compostable plastics in 2022
explanation: The quality standards for the biodegradable and the compostable plastics were notified in 2022, and they are applicable from 1 April 2023 to the products of the large scale producers.

q: The 'India' and the 'Net Zero' commitment:
options: India has committed to the net zero by 2060
India has made no net zero commitment
India has committed to the net zero by 2070
India has committed to the net zero by 2050
explanation: India has committed to the net zero greenhouse gas emissions by 2070 and to the 500 GW of the non-fossil capacity by 2030, and the Panchamrit was announced at the COP26.

q: The 'Panchamrit' of India announced at the COP26 includes:
options: The five pillars of the Panchamrit
The five schemes of the Panchamrit
The five years of the Panchamrit
The five commitments of the Panchamrit
explanation: The Panchamrit is the five-point action plan of India for the environment, with the five commitments on the net zero, the sustainable lifestyles, the green growth, the green hydrogen and the sustainable cities.

q: The 'LiFE' and the 'Bhatt' and the 'BEE' and the 'Panipat':
options: The BEE is a monetary policy tool
The Panipat is a thermal plant
The BEE and the EEE schemes of the energy efficiency were part of the Panchamrit
The Bhatt and the Panipat are the two pilots of the LiFE
explanation: The BEE programme for the energy efficiency in the buildings and the EEE for the appliances are among the initiatives under the Panchamrit.

q: The 'Global Tiger Conservation Programme' and the 'GTCF':
options: The Global Tiger Forum was founded in 2006
The Global Tiger Forum was founded in 1993 and the GTCF was launched in 2006
explanation: The Global Tiger Forum was founded in 1993 and the Global Tiger Conservation Programme was launched in 2006, and the third summit was held in 2022.

q: The 'International Tiger Day' is observed on:
explanation: The International Tiger Day is observed on 29 July to raise the awareness of the tiger conservation, and the year 2022 marked the tenth anniversary of the event.

q: The 'MINI' and the 'Agriculture':
options: The MINI is the National Mission for the Irrigation
The Ministry of Agriculture is the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
The MINI is the National Institute of the Food
The MINI is a scheme of the fisheries
explanation: The Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare is the apex organisation for the agriculture, the rural development and the food processing, and it is the nodal department for the Kisan schemes.

q: The 'Agriculture Infrastructure Fund' was launched in 2020 with a corpus of:
explanation: The Agriculture Infrastructure Fund was launched in August 2020 with a corpus of Rs. 1 lakh crore to finance the post-harvest management infrastructure, and it was extended in 2022.

q: The 'e-NAM' was launched in:
explanation: The electronic National Agricultural Market was launched in April 2016 and it integrated the online trading platforms of the agricultural commodity markets.

q: The 'Kisan Credit Card' was launched in:
explanation: The Kisan Credit Card scheme was launched in 1998, and it was revised in 2019 to include the animal husbandry and the fisheries sectors.

q: The 'PM-KISAN' was launched in:
explanation: The PM-KISAN was launched in February 2019 and it was extended to all the landholding farmer families, including those who had held the land in the past.

q: The 'Agriculture' and the '2021' and the 'UN Food Systems Summit':
options: The UN Food Systems Summit was held in October 2021 in New York
It was held in Rome in 2021
It was held in Rome in 2022
explanation: The UN Food Systems Summit was held in New York in October 2021, and the Five Action Areas included the food security, the nutrition, the sustainable diets and the agri-food innovation.

q: The 'WTO' and the 'MC13' of 2022:
options: The MC13 was held in Bali in 2022
The MC13 was in Doha in 2022
The MC13 was in Cancun in 2022
The MC13 was held in February 2022 in Geneva and it agreed on the food and the agriculture and the services and the intellectual property
explanation: The 13th Ministerial Conference of the WTO was held in Geneva from 9 to 12 February 2022 and it reached the agreement on the agriculture, the food security, the services, the trade facilitation and the intellectual property.

q: The 'WTO' and the 'India's' and the 'dispute settlement':
options: India has never filed a complaint
India cannot be the complainant because of the zero tariff of the developing country status
India is the complainant in the most of the disputes
India was the first complainant in 1995
explanation: The World Trade Organisation's complaint can be made only by a member with a non-zero bound tariff, and hence India as a developing country with the zero tariffs in the agriculture could not be the complainant, and the issue was the subject of the National Implementation Treaty's discussions.

q: The GST compensation to the states have:
explanation: The compensation of the GST revenue loss to the states was originally for five years and it was extended to June 2022 by the 53rd GST Council, and a cess was extended to March 2026 for the health.

q: The '53rd GST Council' meeting of 2022 was held in:
explanation: The 53rd meeting of the GST Council was held on 24 June 2022 in New Delhi, and it extended the compensation to the states and the health cess to March 2026.

q: The 'Fiscal Policy' and the '2022-23' and the 'capital expenditure':
options: The Union Budget of 2022-23 provided for a capital expenditure of Rs. 10 lakh crore
explanation: The Union Budget of 2022-23 provided for a capital expenditure of Rs. 10 lakh crore, about 4.11 per cent of the GDP, with a focus on the logistics and the public capital formation.

q: The 'Union Budget 2021-22' was presented on:
explanation: The Union Budget for 2021-22 was presented on 1 February 2021 by the Finance Minister, and it was the first budget of the second term of the government.

q: The 'Corporate tax' of India was reduced from 30 per cent to:
explanation: The Finance Act of 2021 reduced the corporate tax rate from 30 per cent to 25.17 per cent for the companies that pay the effective tax rate of 25.17 per cent.

q: The inflation target was:
options: retained at 4 per cent with the band of 2 to 6 per cent
explanation: The Monetary Policy Committee continued with the flexible inflation targeting framework and the target of 4 per cent with the band of 2 to 6 per cent.

q: The 'Digital Rupee' or the 'CBDC' pilot was launched in India in:
explanation: The pilot of the digital rupee was launched in November 2022 for the retail use in the selected geographies, and the wholesale version of the CBDC was launched in 2022-23.

q: The 'Account Aggregator' and the 'Sahamati':
options: The Sahamati is the credit information company
The Sahamati is the financial information repository of the Account Aggregator ecosystem in India
The Sahamati is the stock exchange of the depositories
The Sahamati is the digital public infrastructure of the payments
explanation: The Sahamati is the financial information repository that enables the consent-based data sharing for the Account Aggregator in India, and the NUII and the Account Aggregator were launched in 2021.

q: The 'CIBIL' and the 'credit score' and the 'in India:
options: The credit score in India is calculated by the credit information companies on a scale of 300 to 900
It is on a scale of 0 to 100
explanation: The credit score in India is calculated on a scale of 300 to 900 by the credit information companies, and a score above 750 is generally considered good.

q: The 'Insolvency and Bankruptcy' and the '2022' and the 'resolution':
options: The IBC Amendment Act of 2020 was the first significant change in the IBC after 2016
The IBC was amended in 2016 only
explanation: The IBC Amendment Act of 2020 was the first significant change after the enactment in 2016, and it included the restructuring of the financial sector and the establishment of the regulatory bodies.

q: The amalgamation of the City Union Bank, the Andhra Bank and the Corporation Bank was:
explanation: The amalgamation of the City Union Bank, the Andhra Bank and the Corporation Bank was completed in April 2020 to create the Union Bank of India.

q: The Cooperative Societies Act of 2021 was:
options: the first amendment of the Cooperative Societies Act of 2002
explanation: The Cooperative Societies Act of 2021 was the first amendment of the Cooperative Societies Act of 2002 since its enactment, and it covered the Co-operative societies of the multi-state and the cooperative societies of the UT without the legislature.

q: The 'Voting Rights' and the 'women' and the '81st and the 84th Amendment':
options: The 81st Amendment Act of 2000 and the 84th of 2001 provided for the reservation of the seats for the women in the rural and the urban local bodies
The 81st Amendment is about the right to education
The 84th Amendment is about the delimitation
explanation: The 81st and the 84th Amendments provided for the reservation of not less than one-third of the total seats and of the offices of the chairpersons in the Panchayats and the municipalities for the women.

q: The '106th Amendment' of 2021 provided for the reservation of the seats for the women in:
options: The Lok Sabha and the state legislative assemblies
explanation: The 106th Amendment inserted the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam, providing for the reservation of one-third of the seats for the women in the Lok Sabha and in the state legislative assemblies including the Delhi and the Puducherry assemblies.

q: The Supreme Court of India in 2022 was:
options: headed by the Chief Justice Y. V. Chandrachud
headed by the Chief Justice N. V. Ramana
headed by the Chief Justice Dipak Misra
headed by the Chief Justice Ranjan Gogoi
explanation: Justice Y. V. Chandrachud was the Chief Justice of India from November 2022, and the CJI is the senior-most judge of the Supreme Court, the one who is senior in the order of the appointment.

q: The Supreme Court upheld:
options: the abrogation of Article 370 in December 2023
explanation: In December 2023 the Supreme Court upheld the abrogation of the special status of Jammu and Kashmir under Article 370 and directed the restoration of the statehood with the assembly elections in 2024.

q: The 'Article 35A' was inserted in the Constitution by:
explanation: Article 35A was inserted by the Constitution (Nineteenth Amendment) Act, 2010, and it empowered the state legislature to confer on the permanent residents the special rights and the privileges.

q: The '91st Amendment Act' of 2003:
options: Introduced the Goods and Services Tax
Limited the size of the Lok Sabha and the state assemblies to the existing levels
explanation: The 91st Amendment froze the allocation of the seats in the Lok Sabha and the state assemblies at the 1971 census levels until the first census after 2026.

q: Consider the following statements. Which of them is correct with regard to the Article 19(1)(g)?
options: The Supreme Court in 2021 in the M.P. Association of Dealers and the case read the freedom to trade with the reasonableness of the restrictions
explanation: In the M.P. Association of Dealers v. Union of India of 2021, the Supreme Court interpreted Article 19(1)(g) and held that the reasonableness of the restrictions and the consonance with the fundamental rights are the tests.

q: Consider the following statements. Which of them is correct with regard to the Decriminalisation?
options: It was the law on the POCSO
It was the law on the surrogacy
The Criminal Laws (Amendment) Act of 2021 replaced the IPC, the CrPC and the Evidence Act with the BNS, the BNSS and the BSA
explanation: The Criminal Laws (Amendment) Act of 2021 replaced the Indian Penal Code, the Code of Criminal Procedure and the Indian Evidence Act with the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita and the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam.

q: The 'Digital Personal Data Protection Act' was passed by the Parliament in:
explanation: The Digital Personal Data Protection Act was passed in August 2023 and it came into force with the rules in 2025.

q: The 'Telemedicine' and the 'National Telemedicine Board':
options: The National Telemedicine Board is a part of the NMC
The National Telemedicine Board is a separate ministry
The Board is under the CAG
explanation: The National Telemedicine Board was constituted under the Telemedicine Practice Guidelines of 2020 and it is an independent body under the National Medical Commission.

q: The CJI in 2023 was:
explanation: Justice Dhananjaya Y. Chandrachud was the Chief Justice of India from November 2022 to December 2024, and he was the CJI for the G20 summit in 2023.

q: The 'The Chief Election Commissioner' of India in 2022:
explanation: Rajiv Kumar was the Chief Election Commissioner of India from December 2020 to December 2022, and he was succeeded by G. Gopalan in December 2022.

q: Which of the following is correct in the case of the The Election Commission?
options: The ECI mandated the webcasting of the polling stations in the assembly elections in 2022
explanation: The Election Commission mandated the webcasting of the polling stations in the assembly elections in 2022, in the run up to the 2024 general election.

q: The elections to the four Legislative Council seats in 2022 in Maharashtra and Karnataka were:
options: held after the Supreme Court order
explanation: The Supreme Court in 2022 ordered the election to the four vacant Legislative Council seats in Maharashtra and Karnataka and the polling took place in December 2022.

q: The 'The Finance Commission' of India for 2021-26 was chaired by:
explanation: The 15th Finance Commission, chaired by N. K. Singh, was constituted in November 2017 and it submitted its report for 2021-26.

q: The 'The Fifteenth Finance Commission' recommended the devolution of:
options: 41 per cent of the divisible pool to the states
explanation: The 15th Finance Commission recommended the devolution of 41 per cent of the divisible pool to the states, an increase of 6 percentage points over the 14th Commission.

q: The 15th Finance Commission recommended:
options: it did not recommend the health grants
the health grants of Rs. 1 lakh crore
the health grants of Rs. 20,000 crore to the states
the health grants of Rs. 2,000 crore
explanation: The 15th Finance Commission recommended the health grants of Rs. 20,000 crore to the states for the primary health care and it raised the share of the health in the divisible pool.

q: Petroleum products are:
options: in the GST from the start
explanation: The petroleum products have been kept outside the GST and they continue to be governed by the central excise, and the GST Council reviews this periodically.

q: The new tax regime with the lower slabs was:
options: made the default for the taxpayers opting for the new regime
explanation: The Finance Act of 2020 made the new tax regime with the lower slabs and the 87A rebate the default for the individual taxpayers, and it was made available from the assessment year 2021-22.

q: The merchandise exports of India were:
explanation: The merchandise exports of India crossed the $400 billion mark for the first time in 2021-22, and the total exports of the goods and the services were over $680 billion.

q: The reserves crossed:
explanation: The foreign exchange reserves of India crossed the $600 billion mark in 2022 and the reserves were a record high in the fiscal year 2022-23.

q: Which of the following statements is/are correct in relation to the India?
options: The rupee depreciated to a record low of about 82 to the dollar
explanation: The rupee touched a record low of about 82.7 to the dollar in 2022, on the back of the widening of the current account deficit and the outflows.

q: The General Anti-Avoidance Rules were introduced:
explanation: The GAAR, the generalised anti-avoidance rules, were introduced in the Finance Act of 2016 with effect from 1 April 2017, and they target the arrangements that have the effect of avoiding the tax.

q: The Vivad se Vishwas Act of 2020 provided:
options: a scheme for the export promotion
for the direct tax dispute resolution scheme
a scheme for the bank recapitalisation
explanation: The Vivad se Vishwas Act of 2020 provided for the direct tax dispute resolution scheme under which the taxpayers could settle the pending cases at a reduced tax with no interest and no penalty.

q: Consider the following statements. Which of them is correct with regard to the India became?
options: India became the second largest coal producer in the world
explanation: With the coal production of over 850 million tonnes in 2022, India became the second largest coal producer in the world after China.

q: The renewable energy capacity crossed:
explanation: The installed renewable energy capacity of India crossed the 150 GW mark in 2022, and the 2030 target of 500 GW was on track.

q: The India Semiconductor Mission approved:
explanation: The India Semiconductor Mission approved the two fab units, the one by the Micron in Sanand in Gujarat and the one by the Kaynes in the Dholera in 2022-23.

q: The National Quantum Mission was:
explanation: The National Quantum Mission, with an outlay of Rs. 6,003.25 crore, was approved in 2023 for the quantum computers, the communication and the sensing technologies.

q: The National Education Policy of 2020 was:
explanation: The National Education Policy of 2020, which replaced the 30 year old National Education Policy of 1986, was approved by the Cabinet in July 2021.

q: Which of the following is correct in the case of the The National Education Policy?
options: The foundational stage of 3 years, the preparatory of 5 to 8 and the middle of 8 to 11 and the secondary of 11 to 14 and the higher of 14 to 18
It is 5 years of the school and 3 years of the college
It is only for the higher education
explanation: The 5+3+3+4 structure of the NEP covers the foundational stage of three years, the preparatory of five to eight, the middle of eight to eleven, the secondary of eleven to fourteen and the higher secondary of fourteen to eighteen.

q: The medium of instruction till the 5th standard will be:
explanation: The NEP recommends that the medium of instruction till at least the 5th standard will be the mother tongue or the local or the regional language where possible, and the Sanskrit will be offered at the secondary level.

q: Which of the following statements regarding the It emphasises the vocational education is correct?
options: It restricted the vocational education to the urban areas
It made the vocational education optional only for the girls
It emphasises the vocational education with the exposure from the middle school stage
explanation: The NEP emphasises the vocational education with the exposure from the middle school stage and the integration of the vocational education with the mainstream schooling.

q: Which of the following statements regarding the It envisages the multidisciplinary and is correct?
options: It envisages only the research universities
It is only for the school education
It envisages the multidisciplinary and the holistic education with the flexible and the multiple entry and exit points in the academic and the vocational courses
explanation: The NEP envisages a multidisciplinary and holistic education with the flexible and multiple entry and exit points in the academic and the vocational courses.

q: The 75th Independence Day was:
explanation: The 75th Independence Day was celebrated on 15 August 2022 under the theme of 'Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav', and the year 2022 marked the 75th anniversary of the independence.

q: The 'The 'Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav' of 2022-23:
options: Was a year-long celebration of the 75 years of the independence
Was the celebration of the 50 years of the independence
Was the celebration of the 60 years of the republic
Was the celebration of the 100 years of the republic
explanation: The Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav was the year-long commemoration of the 75 years of the independence with 75 events and a series of the thematic programmes.

q: The National Flag Code was:
options: amended in 2021 to specify the day of the hoisting
explanation: The National Flag Code was amended in July 2021, and it now specifies the day of the hoisting of the flag at the schools and the colleges.

q: It was adopted on 26 January 1950 and the Lion Capital of the Sarnath is:
explanation: The State Emblem of India, the Lion Capital of Ashoka at Sanchi, was adopted on 26 January 1950, and the motto Satyameva Jayate comes from the Mundaka Upanishad.

q: Which of the following statements regarding the The National Emblem is correct?
options: The Nandalal Bose designed the National Emblem of India
The Nandalal Bose designed the Ashoka Chakra
The Nandalal Bose designed the Parliament logo
The Nandalal Bose designed the national emblem of Nepal
explanation: The National Emblem of India, adopted on 26 January 1950, was designed by the Nandalal Bose, who was also the principal designer of the national flag.

q: The 'The 15th Lok Sabha' was constituted on:
explanation: The 15th Lok Sabha was constituted on 20 May 2022 after the general election, and the first session began on 13 June 2022.

q: The 'The 17th Lok Sabha' was constituted on:
explanation: The 17th Lok Sabha was constituted on 16 June 2024 after the general election of 2024, and the new government was sworn in on 9 June 2024.

q: The theme of the Economic Survey 2021-22 was:
explanation: The Economic Survey 2021-22 with the theme of Time to Move was presented on 31 January 2022, and the theme of the budget was 'The Budget's Fiscal Policy'.

q: The Five Action Areas included:
options: the food security, the nutrition, the sustainable diets, the agri-food innovation and the resilient food systems
explanation: The Five Action Areas of the UN Food Systems Summit were the food security, the nutritious diets, the sustainable diets, the agri-food innovation and the resilient food systems.

q: In the context of the The, which of the following is correct?
options: The tourism statistics for 2021 showed a recovery in the domestic tourism
The tourism was the highest ever in 2022
The international arrivals were the highest in 2021
The tourism statistics were not published
explanation: The Ministry of Tourism released the India Tourism Statistics 2021 showing the recovery of the domestic tourism with about 677 million visits, and the 2022 statistics showed 1731 million domestic visits.

q: The oil and the gas exploration of the Assam was:
options: opened up to the private players in 2021
explanation: The Assam oil and the gas exploration blocks were opened to the private players in 2021 through the bidding process, after the 2019 and the 2020 explorations.

q: The PLI schemes were announced:
options: for the 14 sectors including the mobile phones, the pharmaceuticals and the food processing
explanation: The government announced the production linked incentive schemes for 14 sectors with an outlay of about Rs. 1.97 lakh crore, and the mobile phones, the pharmaceuticals and the food processing were the prominent among them.

q: The Fund of Funds for Startups was:
options: set up with a corpus of Rs. 10,000 crore
explanation: The Fund of Funds for Startups, set up in 2021 with a corpus of Rs. 10,000 crore, is administered by the SIDBI and it invests in the SEBI registered funds.

q: The National Master Plan has:
options: 14 sectors with the 20 key corridors and the 100 projects
explanation: The PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan has 14 sectors with the 20 key multimodal corridors and about 100 projects to be implemented by 2024-25.

q: Which of the following statements regarding the The National Monetisation Pipeline and is correct?
options: The National Monetisation Pipeline and the National Fund for the strategic sectors
It was the disinvestment of the shares of the PSUs only
It was the privatisation of the airports only
explanation: The government announced the National Monetisation Pipeline and the National Fund for the strategic sectors in 2021 as a part of the fiscal consolidation and the infrastructure development.

q: In the context of the India, which of the following is correct?
options: India hosted the G20 in Bengaluru in 2023
India hosted the G20 in Mumbai in 2023
India hosted the G20 Summit in New Delhi in September 2023
explanation: India hosted the G20 Leaders' Summit in New Delhi on 9 and 10 September 2023 with the theme of One Earth, One Family, One Future.

q: Which of the following is correct in the case of the India hosted?
options: India hosted the Miss World 2023 in Goa
India hosted the Miss World 2017 in Goa
explanation: India hosted the Miss World 2023 in Goa, and the country had earlier hosted the Miss Universe 1994 and the Miss World 2017.

q: The Reliance Retail acquired:
options: the Seven Dreams and the Metro
explanation: In 2022 the Reliance Retail acquired the Seven Dreams and the Metro brands, and the company announced a partnership with the Amazon for the pincode.

q: The e-rupee pilot for the wholesale payments started:
explanation: The wholesale digital rupee pilot was launched in 2022-23 and the retail pilot was in 29 districts of the four states, and the e-rupee is at par with the physical rupee.

q: In the context of the The Quad, which of the following is correct?
options: The Quad announced the trade pact with the EU
The Quad announced the food and the agriculture package with the India-led initiative
The Quad announced the nuclear deal
explanation: The Quad Leaders' Summit in Bali in 2022 announced the food and the agriculture package with the India-led initiative for the resilient food systems.

q: The Water Action Agenda was:
options: announced at the UN Water Conference in New York in March 2023
explanation: The UN Water Conference of 2023 was held in New York and it saw the launch of the Water Action Agenda and the Water Call to Action, and the UN Water Conference of 2016 was in Budapest.

q: The Santiniketan was:
explanation: The Santiniketan, the ashram and the university campus of Rabindranath Tagore, was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage site in July 2023.

q: Which of the following statements regarding the 'Digital India' is correct?
explanation: The Digital India and the digital infrastructure were the key themes of the Digital India Week 2023 and of the Digital Infrastructure Transformation Mission.

q: The 2023 prize went:
options: to Claudia Goldin, James Heckman and Michael Katz, and one of them was the Indian-American Claudia Goldin
explanation: Claudia Goldin, a Harvard economist, was among the three laureates of the 2023 prize in Economic Sciences for their work on the inequality and the institutions.

q: Consider the following statements. Which of them is correct with regard to the India hosted?
options: India hosted the Miss Universe 2021 in Goa
India hosted the Miss Universe 1994 in Goa
explanation: India hosted the Miss Universe 2021 in Goa, and the country hosted the Miss Universe 1994 in Bombay as well.

q: Which of the following statements regarding the 14th President is correct?
options: He was the first from the BJP
He was the 14th President of India and the first from the Dalit community
explanation: Ram Nath Kovind, the 14th President of India from 2017 to 2022, was the first President from the Scheduled Castes and the second Dalit in the office after the K. R. Narayanan.

q: Which of the following statements regarding the 15th President is correct?
options: She is the first woman Chief Minister
She is the Governor of Jharkhand
She is the 15th President of India and the first from the tribal community
explanation: Droupadi Murmu, the 15th President of India since 2022, is the first from the tribal community and the second woman President after Pratibha Patil.

q: The Sengol was the ancient Indian symbol of authority that the President used:
explanation: The Sengol, the ancient Indian symbol of the authority and the sovereignty, was placed on the table of the President for the first time in the 2022 inauguration.

q: The 1 rupee coin with the 250th birth anniversary of the Guru Nanak was:
explanation: The commemorative 1 rupee coin marking the 250th birth anniversary of Guru Nanak was released in 2018, and the 350th anniversary of the Guru Tegh Bahadur was marked in 2016.

q: The 'The 'Mann Ki Baat' is:
options: The monthly radio programme of the Prime Minister that started in 2014
The daily radio show of the President
The monthly show of the Lok Sabha TV
The annual address of the Finance Minister
explanation: Mann Ki Baat, the monthly radio and the TV programme of the Prime Minister broadcast from the Akashvani studio in New Delhi, was first aired in October 2014.

q: The 'The 'Arogya Setu' app was launched in:
explanation: The Aarogya Setu, the contact tracing app for the COVID-19, was launched in April 2020 by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare.

q: In the context of the The Odisha, which of the following is correct?
options: The Kerala was the first to the ODF
The Goa was the first to the ODF
No state has achieved the ODF
The Odisha was the first state to achieve the 100 per cent of the ODF status
explanation: Odisha was the first state to declare itself open defection free with the 100 per cent coverage of the households, and the verification of this was done in 2022.

q: The 'The 'Statue of Unity' and the '2018:
options: The Statue of Unity was inaugurated on 18 October 2018
explanation: The Statue of Unity of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel at Kevadia in Gujarat was inaugurated on 18 October 2018, the 146th birth anniversary of the Sardar.

q: The 'The 'Northeast Frontier Agency' was renamed in:
explanation: The North-East Frontier Agency was renamed the state of Arunachal Pradesh in 1972, and the state was formed on 20 February 1987.

q: In the context of the The Trishul, which of the following is correct?
options: The Trishul was the 1999 Pokhran-II test
The Trishul was the first satellite
The Trishul was the SLV launch vehicle
explanation: Operation Shakti of 1999, the Pokhran-II test, was codenamed Trishul, and the 1974 test was the Smiling Buddha.

q: The 2016 exercise was:
options: the Pokhran test of the artillery and the missiles
explanation: Exercise Nagarjuna, the 2016 test of the missile systems of the Indian Army, was conducted in the Pokhran range.

q: Which of the following statements regarding the The MMM of the ISRO is correct?
options: The MMM was of the China
The MMM of the ISRO and the NASA confirmed the presence of the water in 2009
The MMM was of the ESA only
explanation: The Moon Mineralogy Mapper of the ISRO and the NASA, on the Chandrayaan-1, confirmed the presence of the water molecules on the lunar surface in 2009.
